label: th:Bf
title: Theorem
body_md:
\@gobble{th:Bf}
There exists a smallest finite set $B(f)\subset\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$, called the \@gobble{set!bifurcation --}\emph{bifurcation set of $f$}, such that the map $f^\mathrm{an}:(U\smallsetminus f^{-1}(B(f)))^\mathrm{an}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}\smallsetminus B(f)$ is a $C^\infty$ fibration.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: One chooses a projectivization $f_X:X\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$ of $f$. A theorem of \hbox{Hironaka} \cite{Hironaka77} (see\kern.3em also \cite[Th.\,6.4.5]{L-NB-S20}) asserts that the underlying complex analytic space~$X^\mathrm{an}$ admits a Whitney stratification satisfying Thom's $A_{f_X}$ condition. In fact, in~the quasi-projective context, the strata can be chosen quasi-projective and connected, so that the $f_X$-image of a stratum is either a point or a Zariski dense open set of~$\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$. The construction can be made in order to ensure that $U\smallsetminus f^{-1}(B)$ is a stratum, for some finite set $B$ of $\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$. Thom's first isotopy lemma implies that the restriction of~$f_X$ to each stratum $S$ induces a $C^\infty$ fibration $S^\mathrm{an}\rightarrow f_X(S)^\mathrm{an}$. Applying this to the stratum $U\smallsetminus f^{-1}(B)$ yields the assertion for some (possibly non minimal) finite set~$B$. Minimality can then obviously be achieved.

label: lem:sperv
title: Lemma
body_md:
\@gobble{lem:sperv}
An object $\mathcal{F}$ of $\operatorname{Perv}(\Delta,0;\mathbb{Z})$ belongs to $\operatorname{sPerv}(\Delta,0;\mathbb{Z})$ if and only if the $\mathbb{Z}$-modules ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F})$ and ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})$ are $\mathbb{Z}$-free.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an object of $\operatorname{Perv}(\Delta,0;\mathbb{Z})$. Assume that ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F})$ and ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})$ are $\mathbb{Z}$\nobreakdash-free, and let us prove that $\mathcal{F}$ is an object of $\operatorname{sPerv}(\Delta,0;\mathbb{Z})$. Freeness of ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F})$ as a $\mathbb{Z}$\nobreakdash-mod\-ule is equivalent to the property that the restriction of~$\mathcal{F}$ to the punctured disc~$\Delta^*$ is a \@gobble{sheaf!locally constant --}locally constant sheaf of free $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. According to \cite[Prop.\,10.2.49]{M-S22}, we~are reduced to checking that $\mathcal{H}^0(i_0^!\mathcal{F})$ is free, if~$i_0:\{0\}\mathrel{\lhook\joinrel\rightarrow}\Delta$ denotes the inclusion. The distinguished triangle \cite[(10.90)]{M-S22} reads
\[
i_0^!\mathcal{F}\rightarrow{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4pt\operatorname{Var}_t\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{\operatorname{Var}_t}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F})\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4pt+1\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{+1}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}
\]
and since ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F}),{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})$ are concentrated in degree zero, it leads to the long exact sequence
\[
0\rightarrow\mathcal{H}^0(i_0^!\mathcal{F})\rightarrow{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4pt\operatorname{Var}_t\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{\operatorname{Var}_t}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F})\rightarrow\mathcal{H}^1(i_0^!\mathcal{F})\rightarrow0.
\]
If ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})$ is free, then so is $\mathcal{H}^0(i_0^!\mathcal{F})$.

Conversely, let us assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is an object of $\operatorname{sPerv}(\Delta,0;\mathbb{Z})$. Then the local system (up to a shift) $\mathcal{F}|_{\Delta^*}$ is free, and this implies freeness of ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\psi_t(\mathcal{F})$ and therefore that of $\operatorname{image}(\operatorname{Var}_t)$. The assumption implies that $\mathcal{H}^0(i_0^!\mathcal{F})$ is free, and therefore so is ${}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_t(\mathcal{F})$.

{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_{t-c}(\raisebox{6pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}\!R^k\!f_*A_U)\simeq \raisebox{6pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}\!R^k\!f_{X*}({}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_{f_X-c}(\boldsymbol{R} j_*{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U)),

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $f_X$ is proper, we have identifications
\[
{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_{t-c}(\boldsymbol{R} f_*A_U)\simeq{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_{t-c}(\boldsymbol{R} f_{X*}(\boldsymbol{R} j_*A_U))\simeq\boldsymbol{R} f_{X*}({}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\mkern-1mu\phi_{f_X-c}(\boldsymbol{R} j_*A_U)).

title: Lemma
body_md:
For $t=\rho$ and any $r\geqslant0$, the restriction morphism
\[
\mathrm{H}^r(U,f^{-1}(\rho);A)\rightarrow\mathrm{H}^r(f^{-1}(\Delta_\rho),f^{-1}(\rho);A)

title: Proof
body_md: In view of the exact sequence of relative cohomology, it is enough to show the restriction morphism $\mathrm{H}^r(U;A)\rightarrow\mathrm{H}^r(f^{-1}(\Delta_\rho);A)$ is an isomorphism. By~pushing forward by $f$, we are led to showing a similar result for the hypercohomology of $\boldsymbol{R} f_*A_U$ on $\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$. Let $j:\mathbb{A}^{\!1}\smallsetminus\Delta_\rho\mathrel{\lhook\joinrel\rightarrow}\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$ denote the open inclusion. We are led to showing the vanishing of any hypercohomology space of the complex $\boldsymbol{R} j_!j^{-1}(\boldsymbol{R} f_*A_U)$. Since $j^{-1}(\boldsymbol{R} f_*A_U)$ has \@gobble{sheaf!locally constant --}locally constant cohomology on $\mathbb{A}^{\!1}\smallsetminus\Delta_\rho$ by our assumption on $\rho$, a simple induction reduces the question to the vanishing, for any $r\in\mathbb{N}$, of the cohomology \hbox{$\mathrm{H}^r(\mathbb{A}^{\!1}\smallsetminus\mathaccent"7017\Delta_\rho;j_!\mathcal{L})$} for a locally constant sheaf $\mathcal{L}$ of $A$-modules on $\mathbb{A}^{\!1}\smallsetminus\Delta_\rho$. By~considering the radial projection $\mathbb{A}^{\!1}\smallsetminus\mathaccent"7017\Delta_\rho\rightarrow\partial\Delta_\rho$, this follows from the vanishing of the relative cohomology $\mathrm{H}^r([\rho,+\infty),\{\rho\};A)$ for each $r\in\mathbb{N}$.

label: rem:FirrQ
title: Remark
body_md:
\@gobble{rem:FirrQ}
The \@gobble{filtration!indexed by $\mathbb{Q}$}filtrations $F_{\mathrm{irr},\alpha}^{\raisebox{1pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}}\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)$ and $F_{\mathrm{irr},\alpha}^{\raisebox{1pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}}\mathrm{H}^r_{{\mathrm{dR}},\mathrm{c}}(U,f)$ also have an expression in terms of the \@gobble{complex!twisted meromorphic de~Rham --}\emph{twisted meromorphic de~Rham complex} (see\kern.3em\cite{Yu12}), which makes clear that these filtrations increase with~$\alpha$, so that we can regard all of them as forming a decreasing filtration $F_{\mathrm{irr}}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)$ indexed by $\mathsf{p}=p-\alpha\in-\mathcal{A}+\mathbb{Z}\subset\mathbb{Q}$ by setting
\[
F_{\mathrm{irr}}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)=F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{p-\alpha}\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f):=F_{\mathrm{irr},\alpha}^p\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)
\]
for each $\alpha\in\mathcal{A}$ and $p\in\mathbb{Z}$, and similarly with compact support. This filtration is called the \@gobble{filtration!irregular Hodge --}\emph{irregular Hodge filtration} of $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)$, \text{resp.}\kern.3em $\mathrm{H}^r_{{\mathrm{dR}},\mathrm{c}}(U,f)$. More precisely, J.-D.\,Yu \cite{Yu12} (see\kern.3em also \cite[Cor.\,1.4.5]{E-S-Y13}) considers the complex
\[
0\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{\overline X}\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4pt\mathrm{d}+\mathrm{d} f\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{\mathrm{d}+\mathrm{d} f}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}\Omega^1_{\overline X}(\log D)(\boldsymbol{P})\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow\Omega^d_{\overline X}(\log D)(d\boldsymbol{P})\rightarrow0
\]
filtered by the subcomplexes $F_\mathrm{Yu}^\mathsf{p}$ with $\mathsf{p}\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geqslant0}$:
\begin{multline*}
0\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{\overline X}(\lfloor(-\mathsf{p})_+\boldsymbol{P}\rfloor)\rightarrow\Omega^1_{\overline X}(\log D)(\lfloor(1-\mathsf{p})_+\boldsymbol{P}\rfloor)\rightarrow\cdots\\
\rightarrow\Omega^d_{\overline X}(\log D)(\lfloor(d-\mathsf{p})_+\boldsymbol{P}\rfloor)\rightarrow0,
\end{multline*}
where $(a)_+:=\max(a,0)$ and, for $a\in\mathbb{Q}$, $\lfloor a\boldsymbol{P}\rfloor$ has been defined above. J.\nobreakdash-D.\,Yu shows that $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)$ is the hypercohomology of the latter complex and that $F_\mathrm{irr}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)$ is the filtration induced by the subcomplex $F_\mathrm{Yu}^\mathsf{p}$. As a consequence, we have $\mathrm{gr}^\mathsf{p}_{F_\mathrm{irr}}\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)=0$ for $\mathsf{p}<0$ (the expression in terms of the Kontsevich complex only yields vanishing for $\mathsf{p}\leqslant-1$).

Let us start with Item~\ref{prop:strict1}. Let $I\neq S^1$ be any strict open interval in $S^1$ and assume that a splitting of $\mathscr{L}|_I$ exists, i.e.,\  a morphism $\lambda:\mathop{\textstyle\bigoplus}\displaylimits_c\mathrm{gr}_c\mathscr{L}|_I\stackrel{\sim}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{L}|_I$ compatible with the Stokes filtrations and whose associated graded morphism is the identity. Let us set $C=\{c_1,\dots,c_n\}$ and let $\lambda_i:\mathrm{gr}_{c_i}\mathscr{L}|_I\rightarrow\mathscr{L}_{\leqslant c_i}|_I$ be the restriction of $\lambda$ to $\mathrm{gr}_{c_i}\mathscr{L}|_I$. Another lifting can be obtained as follows. For $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ we denote $j<_Ii$ if $c_j<_\theta c_i$ for any $\theta\in I$. For any $i,j$ with $j<_Ii$, let $\psi_{ji}:\mathrm{gr}_{c_i}\mathscr{L}|_I\rightarrow\mathrm{gr}_{c_j}\mathscr{L}|_I$ be any morphism of (constant) local systems of $A$\nobreakdash-modules. Then $\widetilde\lambda$ with restriction for each $i$ given by $\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i+\sum_{j<_Ii}\lambda_j\circ\psi_{ji}$ defines another splitting on~$I$, and any other splitting on~$I$ is obtained like this. The condition $j<_Ii$ implies that there is no Stokes argument for the pair $(c_i,c_j)$ in $I$. It~follows that, if~$I$ contains one Stokes argument for each pair $(c_i,c_j)$, a splitting on~$I$, if it exists, is unique.

We now show that a splitting exists on any interval $I$ which satisfies:
\par\noindent$(*)$ $I$ contains at most one Stokes argument for each pair $c\neq c'\in C$.
\par\noindent
The proof is by induction on the number of such Stokes arguments in $I$. One first notes that if a splitting exists on~$I$, it can be extended to any $J\supset I$ provided that~$J$ contains the same Stokes argument as~$I$ does. Furthermore, the case of one Stokes argument follows from Item~\ref{def:Stokes3} of Definition \ref{def:Stokes-fillocsys}. Assume then that a splitting~$\lambda$ exists on $I$ satisfying $(*)$ with a boundary point being a Stokes argument $\theta$ such that, if~$I'$ is a small open neighbourhood of $\theta$, $I\cup I'$ still satisfies $(*)$. We will prove that a splitting exists on $I\cup I'$. Let~$\lambda'$ be a splitting of $\mathscr{L}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$ on $I'$ and set $J=I\cap I'$.

Given any $i$ and any $j<_Ji$, we can find $\eta_{ji},\eta'_{ji}:\mathrm{gr}_{c_i}\mathscr{L}_{|J}\rightarrow\mathrm{gr}_{c_j}\mathscr{L}_{|J}$ such that
\[
\lambda'_i|_J=\lambda_i|_J+\sum_{j<_Ji}\lambda_j|_J\circ\eta_{ji}\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_i|_J=\lambda'_i|_J+\sum_{j<_Ji}\lambda'_j|_J\circ\eta'_{ji}.
\]
If $j<_Ji$ and $j\not<_Ii$, then we must have $j<_{I'}i$. We can write
\[
\lambda'_i|_J-\sum_{j<_{I'}i}\lambda_j|_J\circ\eta_{ji}=\lambda_i|_J+\sum_{j<_Ii}\lambda_j|_J\circ\eta_{ji}.
\]
The right-hand side is a new splitting on $I$. In the left-hand side, we use the equality $\lambda_j|_J\circ\eta_{ji}=\lambda'_j\circ\eta_{ji}+\sum_{k<_Jj}\lambda'_k|_J\circ\eta'_{kj}\circ\eta_{ji}$ and we find a new splitting on the left-hand side (but possibly not on the right-hand side)
\begin{multline*}
\lambda'_i|_J-\sum_{j<_{I'}i}\biggl(\lambda'_j|_J\circ\eta_{ji}+\sum_{k<_{I'}j}\lambda'_k|_J\circ\eta'_{kj}\circ\eta_{ji} \biggr)\\
=\lambda_i|_J+\sum_{j<_Ii} \biggl(\lambda_j|_J\circ\eta_{ji}-\sum_{k<_Ij}\lambda'_k|_J\circ\eta'_{kj}\circ\eta_{ji} \biggr).
\end{multline*}
By iterating this process, we get new splittings both on $I'$ and $I$ that coincide on $J$, defining thus a splitting on $I\cup I'$.

For Item \ref{prop:strict2}, we can assume that $(\mathscr{L},\mathscr{L}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})|_I$ and $\mathscr{L}',\mathscr{L}'_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet})|_I$ are graded, according to Item~\ref{prop:strict1}, and write $\lambda=(\lambda_{ji})$ with $\lambda_{ji}:\mathrm{gr}_{c_i}\mathscr{L}|_I\rightarrow\mathrm{gr}_{c_j}\mathscr{L}'|_I$ being constant and zero at any $\theta\in I$ such that $c_j<_\theta c_i$. Since such a $\theta$ exists by assumption on $I$ for any pair $c_i\neq c_j$, it follows that $\lambda|_I$ is diagonal. Then, Item \ref{prop:strict3} follows easily.

title: Proof
body_md: Setting $v=u^{-1}$, it is convenient to first consider the complex $(\Omega^{\raisebox{1pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}}_U[v],\mathrm{d}+v\mathrm{d} f)$, which also comes equipped with an action of $\partial_v$ defined as $\mathrm{e}^{-vf}\circ \partial_v\circ\mathrm{e}^{vf}$. Then $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,vf)$ is a $\mathbb{C}[v]$-module equipped with a compatible action of $\partial_v$, i.e.,\  a module over the Weyl algebra $\mathbb{C}[v]\langle\partial_v\rangle$ of differential operators with polynomial coefficients in the variable $v$. Let us regard $v$ as the derivation $\partial_t$ with respect to the variable $t=-\partial_v$. Regarded as a $\mathbb{C}[t]\langle\partial_t\rangle$-module, $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,vf)$ is interpreted as the $(d-r)$-Gauss-Manin system attached to $f$. The regularity theorem of Griffiths implies that it has a regular singularities at any of its singularity \hbox{$c\in\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$} and also at infinity. A standard theorem of differential equations implies that the $\mathbb{C}[v]\langle\partial_v\rangle$-module $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,vf)$, regarded as the Laplace transform of a $\mathbb{C}[t]\langle\partial_t\rangle$-module with regular singularities, has a regular singularity at $v=0$, an possibly irregular one at $v=\infty$, and no other singularity. The statement of the theorem is obtained by tensoring $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,vf)$ with $\mathbb{C}[u,u^{-1}]=\mathbb{C}[v^{-1},v]$ over $\mathbb{C}[v]$. The assertion on the rank is obtained by identifying the restriction to $u=1$ of the free $\mathbb{C}[u,u^{-1}]$-module $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f/u)$ with $\mathrm{H}^r_{\mathrm{dR}}(U,f)$.

\[
\mathbb{C}[t,1/f']\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4pt\partial_t-f'\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{\partial_t-f'}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}\mathbb{C}[t,1/f']

title: Example
body_md:
Let us illustrate the difference between the $\mathbb{C}(\!( u)\!)$-vector spaces
\[
\mathrm{H}^r\bigl(U,(\Omega_U^{\raisebox{1pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}}(\!( u)\!),\mathrm{d}+\mathrm{d} f/u)\bigr)\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb{C}(\!( u)\!)\otimes_{\mathbb{C}[u,u^{-1}]}\mathrm{H}^r\bigl(U,(\Omega_U^{\raisebox{1pt}{${\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}$}}[u,u^{-1}],\mathrm{d}+\mathrm{d} f/u)\bigr).
\]
Let us take up the notation of Example \ref{ex:HUUan}. Then the formally twisted de~Rham complex
\[
\mathcal{O}(U)(\!( u)\!)\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4ptu\partial_t-f'\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{u\partial_t-f'}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}\mathcal{O}(U)(\!( u)\!)
\]
has cohomology equal to zero. Indeed, let us show for example that the differential is onto. This amounts to showing that, given $\psi_{k_o},\psi_{k_o+1},\dots$ in $\mathbb{C}[t,1/f']$ (with $k_o\in\mathbb{Z}$), we can find $\varphi_{k_o},\varphi_{k_o+1},\dots$ in $\mathbb{C}[t,1/f']$ such that
\[
\psi_{k_o}=-f'\varphi_{k_o},\quad\psi_{k_o+1}=\partial_t\varphi_{k_o}-f'\varphi_{k_o+1},\dots,\psi_{k+1}=\partial_t\varphi_{k}-f'\varphi_{k+1},\dots,
\]
a system which can be solved inductively because $f'$ is invertible in $\mathbb{C}[t,1/f']$.

On the other hand, the complex
\[
\mathbb{C}[t,1/f'][u,u^{-1}]\mathchoice{\xrightarrow{\textstyle\kern4ptu\partial_t-f'\kern3pt}}{\stackrel{u\partial_t-f'}{\longrightarrow}}{}{}\mathbb{C}[t,1/f'][u,u^{-1}]
\]
has cohomology in degree one only, and this cohomology is a free $\mathbb{C}[u,u^{-1}]$-module of rank equal to $\deg f\cdot\#\{f(t)\mid f'(t)=0\}$.

title: Proof
body_md:

Since $F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{>\mathsf{p}}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)$ is a subbundle of $F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{>\mathsf{p}-1}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)$, the composed morphism
\[
i_{u_o}^*F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{>\mathsf{p}}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)\rightarrow i_{u_o}^*F_{\mathrm{irr}}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)\rightarrow i_{u_o}^*F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{>\mathsf{p}-1}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)
\]
is injective. Therefore, $i_{u_o}^*F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{>\mathsf{p}}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)\rightarrow i_{u_o}^*F_{\mathrm{irr}}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)$ is injective and the dimension of $i_{u_o}^*\mathrm{gr}_{F_{\mathrm{irr}}}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)$ is the difference between the ranks of the bundles $F_{\mathrm{irr}}^\mathsf{p}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)$ and $F_{\mathrm{irr}}^{>\mathsf{p}}\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{dR}}^r(U,f/u)$, so is independent of $u_o$. title: Proof
body_md:
The notion of micro-support is useful for explaining the latter property \hbox{(see\kern.3em \cite{K-S90,Dimca04,M-S22})}: Katz' condition is equivalent to the property that the micro-support of the cone $\mathcal{C}$ of the natural morphism $\boldsymbol{R} f_!{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U\rightarrow\boldsymbol{R} f_*{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U$ is reduced to the zero section of the cotangent bundle of $\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$, and this, in turn, is equivalent to the property that its perverse cohomology sheaves are constant. The long exact sequence of perverse cohomology attached to the corresponding distinguished triangle, together with Artin's vanishing result (see\kern.3em \cite[Prop.\,10.3.17]{K-S90} or \cite[Prop.\,5.2.13]{Dimca04}), implies that the assertions of Proposition \ref{propimdirperv} are satisfied, and the converse holds in the same way.

It remains to identify the constant local systems. This is obtained by analyzing the perverse Leray spectral sequence
\[
E_2^{p,q}=\mathrm{H}^p(\mathbb{A}^{\!1},\raisebox{6pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}\!R^qf_*{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U)\implies \mathrm{H}^{p+q}(U,{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U),
\]
and the compact support analogue with $\raisebox{6pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}\!R^qf_!{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U$. Due to the vanishing and constancy statements in Items \ref{propimdirperv1} and \ref{propimdirperv2}, one obtains that it degenerates at $E_2$. Then for $r<d$, the fiber of the shifted constant sheaf $\raisebox{6pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}\!R^{r-d}f_*{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U$, which is isomorphic to $\mathrm{H}^{-1}(\mathbb{A}^{\!1},\raisebox{6pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}$}\!R^{r-d}f_*{}^{\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{p}}\!A_U)$, is thus isomorphic to $\mathrm{H}^{r-1}(U,A_U)$, and we have a similar argument for Item \ref{propimdirperv2}.

A proof for the last assertions can be found in \cite{D-S02a} for M-tameness and in \cite{Bibi97b} for cohomological tameness.

title: Theorem
body_md:

title: Proof

If $f:U\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{\!1}$ is tame, the spectrum of $f$ at infinity is symmetric with respect to $d/2$ and is contained in $[0,d]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first assertion follows from the behavior of spectrum with respect to duality (see\kern.3eme.g.\kern.3em\cite[Prop.\,3.3]{Bibi97b}) or also from the behavior of the irregular Hodge filtration with respect to duality provided by Theorem \ref{th:yuduality} and the identification \eqref{eq:spFirr}. The second assertion follows similarly from the remark after Theorem \ref{th:yuduality} (another argument has been given in \cite{Bibi97b}).

Assume that $f$ is convenient and nondegenerate with respect to its Newton polyhedron. Then the Newton filtration $\mathcal{N}_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet} G_0$ of the Brieskorn lattice coincides with the filtration $V_{\scriptscriptstyle\bullet}(U,f/u)\cap G_0$.
